questions.answerHtml:
Comprehensive reference for Redis commands organized by category with real-world examples for connection testing, key management, and data operations.

Connection & Debugging

Testing Redis Connection with Telnet

Test connectivity to your Redis instance using telnet protocol.

# Install telnet (if not already installed)
sudo apt-get install telnet

# Connect to Redis instance
telnet instance-ip-address 6379

# In the telnet session, enter some Redis commands:
PING                  # Response: PONG
SET HELLO WORLD       # Response: +OK
GET HELLO             # Response: WORLD
DEL HELLO             # Response: :1 (number of deleted keys)
GET HELLO             # Response: $-1 (nil, key doesn't exist)
quit                  # Exit telnet session

Redis CLI Connection

Connect and test Redis using the official redis-cli tool.

# Connect to local Redis instance
redis-cli

# Connect to remote Redis instance
redis-cli -h instance-ip-address -p 6379

# Run command directly without entering CLI
redis-cli -h instance-ip-address PING

# Check connection with password
redis-cli -h instance-ip-address -a your-password PING

Key Management

SET - Store Key-Value

Set a key-value pair with optional expiration.

SET key value              # Set key to value
SET key value EX 3600      # Set with 60-minute expiration
SET key value PX 3600000   # Set with millisecond expiration
SET key value NX           # Set only if key doesn't exist
SET key value XX           # Set only if key exists

GET - Retrieve Value

Retrieve the value of a key.

GET key                    # Get value of key
GET non-existent-key       # Returns nil if key doesn't exist

DEL - Delete Keys

Delete one or more keys.

DEL key1                   # Delete single key
DEL key1 key2 key3         # Delete multiple keys
DEL non-existent-key       # Returns 0 (no keys deleted)

EXISTS - Check Key Existence

Check if one or more keys exist.

EXISTS key1                # Returns 1 if exists, 0 if not
EXISTS key1 key2 key3      # Returns count of existing keys

EXPIRE - Set Key Expiration

Set or modify key expiration time.

EXPIRE key 3600            # Set expiration to 60 minutes
PEXPIRE key 3600000        # Set expiration in milliseconds
TTL key                    # Get remaining time in seconds
PTTL key                   # Get remaining time in milliseconds
PERSIST key                # Remove expiration from key

Data Inspection

KEYS - Find Keys

Search for keys matching a pattern (use with caution in production).

KEYS *                     # List all keys
KEYS user:*                # Find keys starting with "user:"
KEYS *session*             # Find keys containing "session"
DBSIZE                     # Count total number of keys

TYPE - Get Value Type

Check the data type of a key.

TYPE key                   # Returns: string, list, set, zset, hash, etc.

INFO - Server Information

Get Redis server statistics and information.

INFO                       # All server information
INFO server                # Server details
INFO memory                # Memory usage
INFO stats                 # Command statistics
INFO replication           # Master/slave information

References

  • Testing connection of Redis using telnet
  • Redis Official Documentation
  • Redis Commands
  • Google Cloud Memorystore for Redis

questions.question: What are the common Redis caching patterns and strategies?
questions.searchLine: [devops • databases • memory-dbs • redis • commands • reference • database • memory • cache • debugging • caching • patterns • best • practices • pattern] What are the common Redis caching patterns and strategies?
questions.answerText: Redis caching patterns help optimize application performance and data consistency. Common patterns include Cache-Aside, Write-Through, and Write-Behind. Cache-Aside (Lazy Loading) Load data into cache only when necessary. Application checks cache first, and if data is missing, loads from database. 1. Application requests data from cache 2. Cache miss → Application loads from database 3. Application stores data in cache 4. Next requests get data from cache Pros: - Simple to implement - Only cached data is truly relevant - Resilient to cache failures Cons: - Cache misses cause application delay - Stale data possible if database changes - Cache stampede risk (many clients fetch same data) Write-Through Data is written to both cache and database simultaneously. 1. Application writes to cache 2. Cache writes to database (synchronously) 3. Acknowledgment returned to application Pros: - Data consistency guaranteed - Simple to understand - No stale data Cons: - Slower write operations - Write latency depends on database - Wasted cache space for never-read data Write-Behind (Write-Back) Data is written to cache first, database updated asynchronously. 1. Application writes to cache 2. Cache returns immediately (before DB write) 3. Background job writes to database Pros: - Fast write operations - Good for write-heavy workloads - Batches can be optimized Cons: - Risk of data loss if cache fails - Complex to implement correctly - Potential data inconsistency during failures References Caching Patterns - AWS Whitepaper Redis Caching Best Practices Cache Stampede Problem
questions.answerHtml:
Redis caching patterns help optimize application performance and data consistency. Common patterns include Cache-Aside, Write-Through, and Write-Behind.

Cache-Aside (Lazy Loading)

Load data into cache only when necessary. Application checks cache first, and if data is missing, loads from database.

1. Application requests data from cache
2. Cache miss → Application loads from database
3. Application stores data in cache
4. Next requests get data from cache

Pros:

  • Simple to implement
  • Only cached data is truly relevant
  • Resilient to cache failures

Cons:

  • Cache misses cause application delay
  • Stale data possible if database changes
  • Cache stampede risk (many clients fetch same data)

Write-Through

Data is written to both cache and database simultaneously.

1. Application writes to cache
2. Cache writes to database (synchronously)
3. Acknowledgment returned to application

Pros:

  • Data consistency guaranteed
  • Simple to understand
  • No stale data

Cons:

  • Slower write operations
  • Write latency depends on database
  • Wasted cache space for never-read data

Write-Behind (Write-Back)

Data is written to cache first, database updated asynchronously.

1. Application writes to cache
2. Cache returns immediately (before DB write)
3. Background job writes to database

Pros:

  • Fast write operations
  • Good for write-heavy workloads
  • Batches can be optimized

Cons:

  • Risk of data loss if cache fails
  • Complex to implement correctly
  • Potential data inconsistency during failures

References

  • Caching Patterns - AWS Whitepaper
  • Redis Caching Best Practices
  • Cache Stampede Problem

questions.answerHtml:
Comprehensive reference for Git commands organized by category with real-world examples.

Staging & Committing

git add

Add changes from working directory to staging area (Index).

git add <file>          # Stage specific file
git add .               # Stage all changes
git add -A              # Stage all changes including deletions
git add -p              # Stage changes interactively (patch mode)

git commit

Save staged changes as a permanent snapshot with a message.

git commit -m "[Feat] add user authentication"
git commit -am "Update documentation"
git commit --amend                  # Modify the last commit
git commit --amend --no-edit        # Add to last commit without changing message

Viewing Changes

git diff

Compare changes between working directory, staging area, and commits.

git diff                       # Unstaged changes since last commit
git diff --cached              # Staged changes (same as --staged)
git diff --staged              # Staged changes ready to commit
git diff HEAD                  # All changes since last commit
git diff master...contrib      # Changes in contrib branch vs master
git diff --word-diff           # Show changes at word level
git diff <commit1> <commit2>   # Compare two commits

git log

Display commit history with filtering and formatting options.

git log                                      # Full commit history
git log --oneline                            # Condensed format
git log -n 5                                 # Last 5 commits
git log --author=<author>                    # Commits by specific author
git log --since="2 weeks ago"                # Commits since date
git log --until="1 week ago"                 # Commits until date
git log --grep=<pattern>                     # Commits matching pattern
git log --follow <file>                      # History of file (including renames)
git log -p -- <file_path>                    # Changes to specific file
git log A..B                                 # Commits in B but not in A
git log --left-right A...B                   # Commits in A or B but not both
git log --abbrev-commit --no-merges          # Exclude merge commits
git log --pretty="format:%h %G? %aN   %s"   # Show GPG signatures

Branching

git branch

Create, list, and delete branches.

git branch                              # List local branches
git branch -a                           # List all branches (local + remote)
git branch <branch_name>                # Create new branch
git branch -d <branch_name>             # Delete branch (safe)
git branch -D <branch_name>             # Force delete branch
git branch -m <old_name> <new_name>    # Rename branch
git branch --track <branch> origin/<branch>  # Track remote branch

git checkout

Switch branches or restore files.

git checkout <branch>                          # Switch to branch
git checkout -b <branch>                       # Create and switch to branch
git checkout -b <branch> origin/<remote_branch> # Create from remote branch
git checkout -- <file>                         # Discard changes to file
git checkout <commit> -- <file>               # Restore file from commit

git switch

Modern alternative to checkout (Git 2.23+).

git switch <branch>            # Switch to branch
git switch -c <branch>         # Create and switch to branch
git switch -                   # Switch to previous branch

Merging & Rebasing

git merge

Combine branch history into current branch.

git merge <branch>                          # Simple merge
git merge --no-ff <branch>                  # Create merge commit
git merge --no-commit --squash <branch>     # Squash commits into one
git merge --abort                           # Cancel merge with conflicts
git merge --continue                        # Continue merge after resolving conflicts
git merge --strategy-option=ours            # Keep current version on conflicts

git rebase

Reapply commits on top of another branch (rewrites history).

git rebase <branch>                     # Rebase current branch
git rebase -i HEAD~3                    # Interactive rebase last 3 commits
git rebase --continue                   # Continue after resolving conflicts
git rebase --abort                      # Cancel rebase
git rebase --skip                       # Skip current commit during rebase

Stashing

git stash

Temporarily save changes without committing.

git stash                               # Save current changes
git stash save "description"            # Save with description
git stash list                          # List all stashes
git stash pop                           # Apply and remove latest stash
git stash apply stash@{0}              # Apply stash without removing
git stash drop stash@{0}               # Delete specific stash
git stash clear                         # Delete all stashes

Remote Operations

git fetch

Download changes from remote repository (no merge).

git fetch                               # Fetch from default remote
git fetch <remote>                      # Fetch from specific remote
git fetch --all                         # Fetch from all remotes
git fetch origin                        # Fetch from origin
git fetch origin refs/pull/958/head     # Fetch specific pull request
git fetch ../commits.bundle <branch>    # Fetch from bundle file

git pull

Fetch and merge changes from remote (fetch + merge).

git pull                                # Fetch and merge from remote
git pull origin <branch>                # Pull specific branch
git pull --rebase                       # Fetch and rebase instead of merge

git push

Upload commits to remote repository.

git push                                # Push to default remote
git push origin <branch>                # Push specific branch
git push origin --all                   # Push all branches
git push origin --tags                  # Push all tags
git push origin <branch> --force        # Force push (use carefully)
git push -u origin <branch>             # Push and set upstream

git remote

Manage remote repository references.

git remote                              # List remotes
git remote -v                           # List remotes with URLs
git remote add <name> <url>             # Add remote
git remote remove <name>                # Remove remote
git remote rename <old> <new>           # Rename remote
git remote set-url <name> <new_url>     # Change remote URL

History Inspection

git rev-parse

Get commit information and references.

git rev-parse develop                   # Get commit hash for branch
git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD         # Get current branch name
git rev-parse HEAD                      # Get full hash of HEAD

git show

Display specific commit content.

git show <commit>                       # Show commit details
git show <commit>:<file>                # Show file at specific commit

Advanced Operations

git cherry-pick

Apply specific commits to current branch.

git cherry-pick <commit>                # Apply commit
git cherry-pick <commit1> <commit2>     # Apply multiple commits
git cherry-pick <commit>~..<commit>     # Apply range of commits
git cherry-pick --continue              # Continue after resolving conflicts
git cherry-pick --abort                 # Cancel cherry-pick

git bisect

Binary search through commits to find bug introduction.

git bisect start                        # Start bisect session
git bisect bad HEAD                     # Mark current as bad
git bisect good <commit>                # Mark commit as good
git bisect reset                        # Exit bisect mode

git clean

Remove untracked files from working directory.

git clean -n                            # Preview what would be deleted
git clean -f                            # Delete untracked files
git clean -fd                           # Delete untracked files and directories
git clean -fX                           # Delete only ignored files

git archive

Create archive (zip, tar) of project snapshot.

git archive HEAD --format=zip > project.zip
git archive <branch> --format=tar.gz > archive.tar.gz
git archive <branch> --prefix='project/' --format=zip > $(git describe <branch>).zip

git bundle

Package commits for transfer (useful offline).

git bundle create commits.bundle master ^9a466c5
git bundle create repo.bundle HEAD master
git bundle list-heads ../commits.bundle     # List branches in bundle
git bundle verify ../commits.bundle         # Verify bundle validity
git fetch ../commits.bundle <branch>        # Fetch from bundle
git clone repo.bundle repo                  # Clone from bundle

Configuration

git config

Set Git configuration options globally or per-repository.

# Identity
git config --global user.name "Your Name"
git config --global user.email "your@email.com"

# Editor
git config --global core.editor vim
git config --global core.pager less

# Colors
git config --global color.ui true
git config --global color.ui false         # Disable colors

# GPG Signing
git config --global user.signingkey <gpg-key-id>
git config commit.gpgsign true              # Enable signing
git config commit.gpgsign false             # Disable signing
git config --global gpg.program "$(which gpg)"

# Submodules
git config --global submodule.recurse false
git config --global diff.submodule log
git config -f .gitmodules submodule.[name].branch develop

# Aliases (shortcuts)
git config --global alias.co checkout
git config --global alias.br branch
git config --global alias.ci commit
git config --global alias.st status
git config alias.sdiff '!'"git diff && git submodule foreach 'git diff'"
git config alias.spush 'push --recurse-submodules=on-demand'
git config alias.supdate 'submodule update --remote --merge'

# View configuration
git config --list                           # Show all settings
git config --global --list                  # Show global settings
git config --global --edit                  # Edit global config
git config --global --unset <key>          # Unset specific setting

Tags

git tag

Create and manage version tags.

git tag                                 # List all tags
git tag <tag_name>                      # Create lightweight tag
git tag -a <tag_name> -m "message"     # Create annotated tag
git tag -a v1.2 9fceb02                # Tag specific commit
git tag -d <tag_name>                  # Delete tag locally
git push origin <tag_name>              # Push specific tag
git push origin --tags                  # Push all tags

Undoing Changes

Undo Strategies

# Discard changes (unstaged)
git checkout -- <file>
git restore <file>                      # Modern syntax

# Unstage changes
git reset HEAD <file>
git restore --staged <file>             # Modern syntax

# Undo last commit (keep changes)
git reset --soft HEAD~1

# Undo last commit (discard changes)
git reset --hard HEAD~1

# Revert specific commit (create new commit)
git revert <commit>

# Revert to specific commit
git reset --hard <commit>

Useful Patterns

Check what needs to be merged

git log --abbrev-commit --no-merges your_branch..origin/master
git log -n <number> your_branch..origin/master

See remote references

git ls-remote                           # All refs
git ls-remote | grep pull               # Pull requests
git ls-remote origin                    # Branch refs

Track remote branch

git checkout -b [local_branch] [remote]/[branch]
git branch --track <branch> origin/<branch>

Sync with remote after others pushed

git fetch origin
git merge origin/master
git push

View all changes before push

git diff --cached HEAD
git log origin/master..HEAD             # Commits not in remote

Best Practices

  1. Commit often - Logical, atomic commits are easier to review and debug
  2. Write meaningful messages - Follow commit message conventions
  3. Pull before push - Sync with remote before pushing
  4. Use branches - Develop features on separate branches
  5. Review before committing - Use git diff to verify changes
  6. Clean up branches - Delete merged branches to keep repo tidy
  7. Sign commits - Use GPG signing for security
  8. Use tags for releases - Annotated tags for production versions
  9. Document workflow - Keep team aligned on branching strategy
  10. Backup before force push - --force rewrites history, be careful

Common Workflows

Feature Branch Workflow

git checkout -b feature/my-feature       # Create feature branch
# Make changes...
git add .
git commit -m "[Feat] implement feature"
git push -u origin feature/my-feature
# Create pull request
# After review and merge:
git checkout main
git pull origin main
git branch -d feature/my-feature

Release Branch Workflow

git checkout -b release/v1.0             # Create release branch
# Fix bugs only
git commit -m "[Fix] critical bug"
git push origin release/v1.0
# After testing:
git checkout main
git merge --no-ff release/v1.0
git tag -a v1.0 -m "Release v1.0"
git push origin main --tags

Hotfix Workflow

git checkout -b hotfix/critical-bug      # Branch from main
git commit -m "[Fix] critical production issue"
git push origin hotfix/critical-bug
# Create pull request
# After merge and testing:
git tag -a v1.0.1 -m "Hotfix v1.0.1"
git push origin v1.0.1

questions.answerHtml:
Follow these conventions for clear, searchable, and maintainable commit history.

Commit Message Format

<type>(<scope>): <subject>

<body>

<footer>

Commit Types

[Add] - New addition

Use when introducing new files or features that don't fit other categories.

git commit -m "[Add] new user authentication module"
git commit -m "[Add] database migration script for schema v2"
git commit -m "[Add] API endpoint for user profile"

[Build] - Build system changes

Changes affecting the build, CI/CD pipelines, or external dependencies.

git commit -m "[Build] update webpack configuration for production"
git commit -m "[Build] configure GitHub Actions workflow"
git commit -m "[Build] add Docker build multi-stage optimization"

[Chore] - Dependency updates

Updates to dependencies, tooling, or maintenance tasks.

git commit -m "[Chore] upgrade npm dependencies to latest versions"
git commit -m "[Chore] update Python package requirements"
git commit -m "[Chore] bump Node.js version to 18.x"

[CiCd] - CI/CD pipeline changes

Continuous integration and continuous delivery related changes.

git commit -m "[CiCd] add automated deployment pipeline"
git commit -m "[CiCd] configure test coverage reporting"
git commit -m "[CiCd] add pre-commit linting hooks"

[Docs] - Documentation updates

Updates to README, markdown files, or code comments.

git commit -m "[Docs] update installation instructions in README"
git commit -m "[Docs] add API documentation for authentication"
git commit -m "[Docs] improve code comments for utility functions"

[Feat] - New feature

A new feature is introduced with the changes.

git commit -m "[Feat] implement dark mode toggle"
git commit -m "[Feat] add search functionality with filters"
git commit -m "[Feat] support OAuth2 authentication"

[Fix] - Bug fix

A bug fix has occurred.

git commit -m "[Fix] resolve memory leak in event listener cleanup"
git commit -m "[Fix] correct calculation in billing module"
git commit -m "[Fix] handle null reference in data parser"

[Improvement] - Enhancement

Improvements or enhancements to existing functionality.

git commit -m "[Improvement] enhance search performance with caching"
git commit -m "[Improvement] optimize database queries for reports"
git commit -m "[Improvement] streamline user onboarding flow"

[Perf] - Performance improvements

Optimizations that improve speed or resource usage.

git commit -m "[Perf] reduce bundle size by 40%"
git commit -m "[Perf] optimize image loading with lazy loading"
git commit -m "[Perf] cache API responses for 5 minutes"

[Refactor] - Code refactoring

Refactored code that neither fixes a bug nor adds a feature.

git commit -m "[Refactor] extract duplicate logic into helper functions"
git commit -m "[Refactor] simplify conditional statements with early returns"
git commit -m "[Refactor] reorganize module structure for clarity"

[Release] - Release notes

Version release or release-related changes.

git commit -m "[Release] v1.2.0 - add authentication and performance improvements"
git commit -m "[Release] v2.0.0 - breaking: migrate to new API schema"

[Remove] - Removal

Remove functions, temporary files, deprecated code, or unused features.

git commit -m "[Remove] delete deprecated API endpoints"
git commit -m "[Remove] clean up temporary test fixtures"
git commit -m "[Remove] remove legacy browser compatibility code"

[Revert] - Revert previous commit

Reverts a previous commit (use sparingly, prefer explicit fixes).

git commit -m "[Revert] revert '[Feat] add A/B testing feature' (caused production issue)"
git commit -m "[Revert] revert commit abc1234 due to merge conflict"

[Style] - Code formatting

Related to code formatting such as whitespace, missing semi-colons, and similar cosmetic changes.

git commit -m "[Style] format code with Prettier"
git commit -m "[Style] add missing semicolons"
git commit -m "[Style] adjust indentation for consistency"

[Test] - Testing changes

Including new, correcting previous, or improving tests.

git commit -m "[Test] add unit tests for payment module"
git commit -m "[Test] fix flaky integration test for API"
git commit -m "[Test] increase test coverage to 85%"

[Update] - General updates

General updates or changes that don't fit specific categories.

git commit -m "[Update] change user profile default avatar"
git commit -m "[Update] modify configuration for staging environment"
git commit -m "[Update] refresh vendor libraries"

Best Practices

  1. Use imperative mood - "add feature" not "added feature"
  2. Keep subject line under 50 characters - Concise and scannable
  3. Separate subject from body with blank line - Easier to read in logs
  4. Wrap body at 72 characters - Better formatted in terminals
  5. Explain what and why, not how - Implementation details should be clear from code
  6. Use lowercase for type - Consistency across commits
  7. No period at end of subject - Convention in many projects
  8. Reference issues and PRs - Link to tracking systems: "Fixes #123" or "Relates to PR #456"

Extended Commit Example

git commit -m "[Feat] add OAuth2 authentication support

- Implement Google OAuth2 provider integration
- Add JWT token generation and validation
- Support refresh token rotation for security
- Create user session management module

Closes #234
Relates to milestone v2.0

Conventional Commits Standard

For stricter formatting, use Conventional Commits format:

git commit -m "feat(auth): add OAuth2 support

Implement OAuth2 authentication with Google provider.
Supports automatic token refresh and secure session handling.

BREAKING CHANGE: Legacy token format is no longer supported
Closes #234

Commit Frequency

  • Frequent, logical commits - One feature/fix per commit when possible
  • Atomic changes - Each commit should be independently deployable
  • Meaningful history - Commits tell a story of development decisions

Tools to Help

  • commitizen - Interactive commit message generator
  • husky + lint-staged - Enforce commit message standards
  • conventional-commits - Strict format validation
  • git-aliases - Create shortcuts for common patterns

Example .gitconfig alias:

git config --global alias.feat '!git commit -m "[Feat]"'
git config --global alias.fix '!git commit -m "[Fix]"'
git config --global alias.docs '!git commit -m "[Docs]"'

Usage: ``bash git feat "add new login form" # [Feat] add new login form git fix "handle null pointer" # [Fix] handle null pointer git docs "update API reference" # [Docs] update API reference ``

questions.answerHtml:
Comprehensive reference for Windows Command Prompt and PowerShell commands organized by category for system administration, diagnostics, and troubleshooting.

System Information & Health

systeminfo

Display detailed system configuration and hardware information.

systeminfo                                          # Show all system info
systeminfo | findstr /C:"OS Name"                  # Show Windows version
wmic os get caption                                 # Get Windows edition
wmic cpu get name                                   # Show CPU model
wmic cpu get NumberOfCores                          # Show CPU cores
wmic memorychip get capacity                        # Show RAM modules
Get-ComputerInfo                                    # PowerShell system info

System File Checker (sfc)

Scan and repair corrupted system files.

sfc /scannow                                        # Scan and repair system files
sfc /verifyonly                                     # Scan without repair
sfc /scanfile=<filepath>                           # Scan specific file

DISM (Deployment Image Servicing Management)

Repair Windows component store and image health.

DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /CheckHealth           # Quick health check
DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /ScanHealth            # Detailed scan
DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth         # Repair Windows components
DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /StartComponentCleanup # Clean up old components

chkdsk

Check disk for errors and bad sectors.

chkdsk C:                                           # Check disk (read-only)
chkdsk C: /F                                        # Fix errors on next boot
chkdsk C: /F /R                                     # Scan and repair bad sectors
chkdsk C: /V                                        # Verbose output

Event Logs & Monitoring

Event Logging Tools

View and manage Windows Event Log channels.

wevtutil el                                         # List all event log channels
wevtutil qe System /c:20 /f:text                   # Show last 20 system events
wevtutil cl System                                  # Clear System log
Get-EventLog -LogName System -Newest 50             # PowerShell: last 50 system logs
Get-WinEvent -LogName Security -MaxEvents 20       # PowerShell: security logs
Get-WinEvent -FilterHashtable @{LogName='System'; Level=2}  # Error events only

Performance Counters

Monitor real-time system performance metrics.

Get-Counter '\Processor(_Total)\% Processor Time'  # CPU usage
Get-Counter '\Memory\Available MBytes'              # Available RAM
Get-Counter '\Memory\% Committed Bytes In Use'     # Memory utilization
Get-Counter '\Network Interface(*)\Bytes Total/sec' # Network throughput
Get-Counter '\LogicalDisk(C:)\% Disk Time'        # Disk usage
typeperf -cf counters.txt -o output.csv            # Log performance over time

Process Management

tasklist & taskkill

View and terminate running processes.

tasklist                                            # List running processes
tasklist /v                                         # Detailed process list
tasklist /v | findstr python                       # Find specific process
taskkill /PID 1234 /F                              # Kill by PID (force)
taskkill /IM notepad.exe /F                        # Kill by name
Get-Process                                         # PowerShell: list processes
Get-Process | Sort-Object CPU -Descending          # Top CPU consumers
Get-Process | Sort-Object WorkingSet -Descending   # Top RAM consumers
Stop-Process -Name notepad -Force                  # PowerShell: kill process

Services Management

sc (Service Control)

Manage Windows services from command line.

sc query                                            # List all services
sc query <service>                                  # Check specific service
sc start <service>                                  # Start service
sc stop <service>                                   # Stop service
sc config <service> start= auto                    # Auto-start on boot
sc config <service> start= demand                  # Manual start
sc config <service> start= disabled                # Disable service
sc delete <service>                                 # Delete service
sc query state= all                                # List all services (any state)

PowerShell Service Cmdlets

Manage services with PowerShell.

Get-Service                                         # List all services
Get-Service -Name <service>                        # Get specific service
Start-Service -Name <service>                      # Start service
Stop-Service -Name <service>                       # Stop service
Restart-Service -Name <service>                    # Restart service
Set-Service -Name <service> -StartupType Automatic # Set auto-start

Drivers Management

Driver Query & Management

List and manage installed drivers.

driverquery                                         # List drivers
driverquery /v                                      # Detailed driver info
driverquery /si                                     # Driver signing info
pnputil /enum-drivers                              # List driver packages
pnputil /delete-driver oem12.inf /uninstall       # Remove driver package
Get-WmiObject Win32_SystemDriver                   # PowerShell: system drivers

Networking

ipconfig

Display and configure network settings.

ipconfig                                            # Show IP configuration
ipconfig /all                                       # Full network details
ipconfig /renew                                     # Renew DHCP lease
ipconfig /flushdns                                  # Clear DNS cache
ipconfig /registerdns                              # Register DNS with domain
ipconfig /release                                  # Release DHCP lease
Get-NetIPAddress                                    # PowerShell: IP addresses
Get-NetAdapter                                      # Show network adapters

Connectivity Testing

Test network connectivity and DNS resolution.

ping hostname                                       # Test connectivity
ping 8.8.8.8                                        # Test internet connectivity
tracert hostname                                    # Trace network route
tracert -d hostname                                 # Trace (IP only)
nslookup hostname                                   # DNS lookup
nslookup -type=MX domain.com                       # Query MX records
